Creative Arts
Creative Arts at Bromstone
Creative Arts develops emotional intelligence, confidence and resilience, discipline and commitment and communications skills. Bromstone has a very active Choir and Musical Theatre Club who perform regularly for the school and local community.
The Royal Shakespeare Associate School
Bromstone has been lucky enough to be a Royal Shakespeare Associate School this year, taking part in an amazing opportunity to explore Shakespeare’s plays. This year, this has been done through Shakespeare club, where a select few year 5 children have learnt a small section of the play ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ and will be performing it on stage at the Marlowe Theatre with 10 other schools!
Creating music for the performance with an RSC musician in December!

pageCache.text:
Information for New Starters
Welcome to Bromstone! We are delighted you have chosen our School.
On your child's first day, please bring them to the school office, where the class teacher will come to welcome you and take your child round to class.
Your child will then enter and leave the school via the school gates. Collection information can be found on the 'Key Information' page: Click here.
We offer hot and cold lunch every day for £2.50. Your child can choose in advance or on the day which they would prefer, alternatively they can bring their own lunch from home. The class teacher will take a dinner register in the morning. Menus can be found on the School Meals page.
If you think your children maybe eligible for free school meals please complete the online form or contact the School Office.
We offer many varied after school clubs. Most of these are free, except for After School Club which runs from 3-5.30pm on Monday - Thursday, and 3-4pm on Friday for £3.25 an hour. The club timetable can be found here. If your child wishes to join a club, bookings can be made via Arbor.
Once your child is enrolled at Bromstone, parents will be sent a link to our online booking system. All communication from the school will be sent via the Arbor parent app and email service and all bookings and payments made via Arbor. We do not accept cash in school.
Our uniform can be purchased from 'The Schoolwear Centre' in Margate. Full details can be found here. We also sell good quality, second hand uniform in the office and through Arbor.
We email weekly and termly newsletters to all families. The newsletters include lots of information about what is happening at Bromstone. To read our most recent newsletters, please follow this link.
Our school calendar is up-to-date with all the exciting activities we have planned throughout the academic year; please ensure you check this regularly. Click here to visit our school calendar.
Each year group has its own page on the website, with information about the term's learning, staff members and any dates or activities relevant to each individual class. Class pages can be found here.
If your child has a medical condition or allergy, please refer to the section on our website Supporting Children with Medical and Dietary Needs for further information.
We look forward to welcoming you and your child into the Bromstone family. If you have any questions, please contact the office on 01843 867010 or via office@bromstone.kent.sch.uk.
Information for New Starters

Governors
Governors of the Bromstone Primary School & St Mildred's Infant Primary School Federation
Governors - What we do
A governing board and its governors must, as required by The School Governance (Roles, Procedures and Allowances) (England) Regulations 2013, regulation 6(2):
The governing board also has legislative responsibility and strategic oversight for the school’s safeguarding arrangements.
The core functions of the governing board are as set out in (regulation 6) and include, but are not limited to ensuring:
As Governors of St Mildred's & Bromstone together with the Executive Headteacher we make important decisions on how the schools are run. We are here to ensure that every child in the schools achieve the best possible outcome during their time in our schools.
We make decisions on policy and strategy for the schools and are accountable to parents and carers as well as the wider community and Ofsted.
The Governing Board:
The full Governing board meets 5 times per year and we have two committees that also meet 3 times a year. These committees are Quality of Education and Leadership & Management. The Leadership & Management committee has responsibility for oversight of the financial management of the school as well as the staffing structure and personnel issues.
As well as the meetings, the governors will visit the school throughout the year to gather data to assess the results of improvements which have been implemented or to look at specific subjects or areas of school life.
We often attend school events throughout the year, so please feel free to say hello, ask us questions about the school and give us your views.
The Chair of Governors can be contacted via the school office.

Learning Powers
At Bromstone we think it is very important that children understand that they are learners and that they have a role to play as a learner.
We therefore believe that children should be taught how to learn and that there are certain skills they can develop which will mean they are more effective and successful lifelong learners. We have developed a set of 'learning powers' with the children and these help them to become better learners.

SEND
Special Educational Needs (SEN) and Disability Information
Our SEN Information Report – which is part of Kent County Council’s Local Offer – provides details about how we support children and young people with Special Educational Needs in our school.
The SEN Information Report was reviewed and updated in September 2020.
At Bromstone Primary School, we are committed to the equal inclusion of all pupils in all areas of school life. We recognise the diverse and individual needs of all of our pupils and take into account the additional support required by those children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
At Bromstone Primary School we ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs make the best possible progress.
This SEND Information Report should be read alongside the school’s SEND Policy, the Equalities Information and Objectives and the Accessibility Plan.
Choosing a new school for your child is one of the most important decisions you have to make as a parent and we hope that we will be your first choice. You are more than welcome to visit us at Bromstone Primary school before you make your decision. Please contact the school office to make an appointment.
The Local Authority oversee all admission arrangements for our school including admission arrangements for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). All information can be found using the links at the bottom of this page.
We are committed to meeting the needs of all children including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. We would ask parents to discuss the identified needs with the school prior to starting so that appropriate intervention and support can be planned and implemented. Advice from the LA or other agencies may be requested to ensure any the school can meet any needs appropriately.

Should you need to contact After School Club after schools hours please contact 07525855486.

After School Clubs

Curriculum
Statement of Intent
At Bromstone our nurturing approach to the curriculum is designed so each child can develop confidence, independence and curiosity in a safe environment.
Our curriculum is child centred and we ensure the curriculum is relevant, current and motivating for all involved.
We encourage our children to develop skills that will enable children to make decisions, self-regulate, and make connections with the world around them.
We want our pupils to be become lifelong learners. During learning opportunities, children acquire key skills, knowledge, concepts and values.
We use Learning Powers to promote responsibility for learning and future success.
In addition, the curriculum is supported by our school values and vision, where mutual respect is essential. We aim for pupils to respect themselves and acknowledge their own self-worth.
As our children journey through our enriched and creative curriculum, we will build upon prior learning and provide a breadth of experiences.
This will enable the children to become creative and confident, critical thinkers who will challenge and ask questions.
Language is a vital means of communication, and we encourage our children to have a voice. A voice that is listened to, appreciated and respected.
Outdoor learning opportunities are given at every opportunity. Our learning environments, wherever they are, set out to inspire and enable learning.
Childhood should be a happy, investigative and enquiring time in our lives where there are no limits to curiosity and there is a thirst for new experiences and knowledge.
Our aim is that when children leave Bromstone, they are prepared for the many challenges they will face, as they become future citizens of the world. We appreciate the importance of transition in children's lives.
We hope they will illustrate positive attitudes to learning which reflect the values and skills needed to promote responsibility for learning and future achievements.
A Bromstone children will have high aspirations and become the very best version of themselves as they take their next steps within education and the wider community.
Dream, Believe, Achieve.

pageCache.text:
Bromstone is 50 years old
This year we celebrate 50 years of Bromstone Primary School. Throughout the school year we will be celebrating this occasion. During the week of 15th September we will have a week of activities and celebrations to mark the occasion. In term 2 we will be opening our school to ex staff and pupils for tea and tours.
